rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies a different alloy system (WTaTiVZr vs. HfZrTi(TaNbV)x) and compares it to pure tungsten, whereas the hidden target adds Ta, Nb, and V to HfZrTi to form a series of alloys and compares them to the base HfZrTi. This is a completely different kind of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses quasi-static compression at 0.001 s^-1, indentation plastometry up to 500 °C, and scratch testing, while the hidden target uses quasi-static tension/compression and SHPB dynamic compression at 4000 s^-1 in air. The conditions are entirely different, with no overlap in testing regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and improved plasticity via Ti, V, Zr, whereas the hidden target's mechanism involves BCC stabilization by Ta, Nb, V, suppression of HCP/omega phases, adiabatic heating leading to shear banding, and fragmentation-induced oxidation energy release. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher strength, greater plastic strain, lower BDTT, and higher fracture toughness relative to pure tungsten, while the hidden target predicts increased strength, retained ductility, and enhanced dynamic energy release relative to HfZrTi. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
